item.title: Fiji Airways may not replace some departing staff as AI improves efficiency “ Scurrah
item.description: Fiji Airways may not need to replace some employees who leave the airline as it introduces artificial intelligence to improve efficiency and reduce high operating costs. Speaking on fijivillage Straight Talk with Vijay Narayan, Fiji Airways CEO and Managing Director Paul Scurrah says the airline employs about 2,200 people and is reviewing its staffing levels and organisational structure as part of
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Airways may not need to replace some employees who leave the airline as it introduces artificial intelligence to improve efficiency and reduce high operating costs.

Speaking on fijivillage Straight Talk with Vijay Narayan, Fiji Airways CEO and Managing Director Paul Scurrah says the airline employs about 2,200 people and is reviewing its staffing levels and organisational structure as part of efforts to achieve financial sustainability.

Scurrah acknowledges that some areas of the business may have more staff than needed and says the airline is looking at ways to operate more efficiently.

He says Fiji Airways still relies heavily on manual processes and is investing in technology to improve productivity.

Scurrah says artificial intelligence could take over some routine tasks, allowing employees to focus on more meaningful work.

However, he acknowledges that as technology improves, the airline may not need to fill some vacancies when employees leave.

Scurrah stresses that this does not mean Fiji Airways is planning widespread job cuts because of artificial intelligence.

He says any decisions affecting employees will be made carefully and respectfully.

Meanwhile, Scurrah says Fiji Airways plans to introduce an additional 125,000 passenger seats in 2027, which is expected to increase operational demand and provide opportunities to make better use of its existing workforce.

He says the staffing review forms part of wider cost-reduction efforts across the airline, including property rentals, procurement and catering.

Scurrah stresses that Fiji Airways must become financially sustainable while continuing to provide reliable services to its customers.

item.title: Diwali firecracker incidents in Davuilevu and Cunningham raise concerns over children's behaviour and public safety
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 11/11/2026 Serious concerns have been raised about the deplorable behaviour of some children during Diwali celebrations this year, with two videos being widely shared on social media showing children involved in the incidents.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 11/11/2026

Serious concerns have been raised about the deplorable behaviour of some children during Diwali celebrations this year, with two videos being widely shared on social media showing children involved in the incidents.

A video shared by a family from Davuilevu shows some children throwing firecrackers when the family was celebrating Diwali at their home.

This has raised serious concerns about the safety and security of families celebrating cultural occasions with their loved ones.

The video shows family members sharing a basin of kava when firecrackers were thrown inside their house.

The family has reported the incident to the Nakasi Police Station. However, they say no action was taken and Police did not respond to their report.

There was also an incident at Cunningham Stage 4, where some children threw firecrackers inside a shop.

Meanwhile, Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs Lenora Qereqeretabua is urging iTaukei parents to take greater responsibility for their children's behaviour.

She is deeply embarrassed by reports of what is happening in some iTaukei communities and whether parents are doing enough to instil discipline and respect in their children.

She questions where discipline, respect and parental guidance have gone, and whether parents are spending more time on their phones than looking after their children.

The Assistant Minister is challenging iTaukei parents who proudly speak about their Vanua, religion and culture to reflect on whether they are practising the values they claim to uphold.

She also questions calls for Fiji to become a Christian state, saying parents should first examine their own behaviour and the example they are setting for their children.

Qereqeretabua stresses the importance of parental responsibility in teaching children discipline, respect and values that promote peaceful coexistence in Fiji's multicultural society.

We have sent questions to Police regarding the two incidents, but they have yet to respond.

item.title: Four critical bridges to be replaced under $175m resilience project
item.description: Four critical bridges along the Queen's Road corridor will be replaced, in a move expected to improve the safety and reliability of travel for thousands of people who depend on the busy route. The replacement works will be carried out under the Critical Bridges Resilience Programme (CBRP), following the signing of construction contracts worth approximately $175 million with contracts been awarded
item.content:encoded:
Four critical bridges along the Queen's Road corridor will be replaced, in a move expected to improve the safety and reliability of travel for thousands of people who depend on the busy route.

The replacement works will be carried out under the Critical Bridges Resilience Programme (CBRP), following the signing of construction contracts worth approximately $175 million with contracts been awarded to a joint venture between China Railway First Group Company Limited and China Railway No. 5 Engineering Group Company Limited.

Speaking at the contract signing ceremony, Minister for Public Works Ro Filipe Tuisawau says the bridges play an important role in connecting communities and supporting the movement of people and goods.

He says the Queen's Road corridor supports key economic activities, including tourism, agriculture, industries and businesses.

Ro Filipe says Fiji continues to face the impacts of tropical cyclones and intense rainfall, making it important to ensure the country's infrastructure is resilient to future disasters.

He says design flood clearances, seismic protection and other safety measures have been taken into account in the project.

The project has been divided into two contract packages.

Package A covers the replacement of the Lami and Medraukutu bridges, with an awarded contract value of approximately $90 million.

Package B covers the replacement of the Visesei and Sabeto bridges, with an awarded contract value of approximately $85 million.

Ro Filipe says the Government, through the Fiji Roads Authority, expects the works to be delivered in accordance with approved designs, contractual requirements and agreed implementation schedules.

Meanwhile, Asian Development Bank Country Operations Head Matthew Rees says the project is an important milestone in the partnership between the Government, the Fiji Roads Authority, ADB and the World Bank.

Rees says the programme also aims to strengthen the Fiji Roads Authority's institutional capacity, identify climate solutions and promote gender equality and inclusion in the transport sector.

He says the project has four key outcomes, including replacing critical bridges with resilient structures, strengthening the capacity of the Fiji Roads Authority, identifying and preparing climate solutions, and implementing gender policies and action plans.

Rees says continued cooperation between the Fiji Roads Authority, contractors, construction supervision consultants, ADB and the World Bank will be important to ensure the works are delivered safely, to a high standard, on time and within budget.
